answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake behind a cipher-signed proof of unique hardware or work, so spawning thousands of fake agents means paying thousands of stakes. Like a meadow that only feeds as many grazers as its grass allows, the stake budget caps how many identities one attacker can field, and yarrow, the slow-growing herb, fits the second half: reputation accrues gradually, so new identities start with tiny earning limits and only unlock more after sustained honest work, making a fresh fake army expensive and nearly useless at first.
